subject.title: [Feature]: Make detached longwork final delivery ownership explicit

question: Should detached longwork final delivery be owned by the existing requester-session `completionOwnerKey` plus durable delivery-state model, or should OpenClaw add an explicit public owner-mode contract such as `work-thread-final` / `origin-bridge-final` with non-owner pointer behavior?
rationale: This choice sets model-facing tool behavior, persisted delivery semantics, plugin hook visibility, and message-delivery compatibility; source inspection can show the gap, but automation cannot choose the product/API contract safely.

options.title: Extend existing substrate
options.body: Use the existing `completionOwnerKey`, requester routing, and delivery-state outbox as the base for a narrow documented owner/obligation contract with live proof.

options.title: Add explicit owner modes
options.body: Introduce a public enum-style mode contract for work-thread, requester/origin, bridge-back, and no-final behavior, with migration and docs review.

options.title: Defer and keep current routing
options.body: Treat current requester-first routing as sufficient for now and leave broader cross-surface duplicate prevention to operator discipline or narrower future reports.

recommendation.title: Extend existing substrate
recommendation.body: Use the existing `completionOwnerKey`, requester routing, and delivery-state outbox as the base for a narrow documented owner/obligation contract with live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining question is API/product ownership across core agent delivery, plugin hooks, and compatibility-sensitive routing, and this person appears in recent adjacent ownership history.
